sub.help: Plain-English answers to common questions. When Sweepwise goes public, you can also ask on GitHub, where questions are answered in public so the next person finds the answer too.
help.1.a: It clears temporary files and caches that Windows and your apps make and never tidy up, runs a quick Windows Security virus scan and checks your PC's health. Then it lists anything else it suggests (files to tidy, old AI leftovers, startup programs, unused programs) and waits for your OK. The very first time, it shows what it would remove and waits for you to press Clean now.
help.2.q: Can Sweepwise delete my personal files?
help.2.a: No. Safe cleaning only touches temporary files and caches in a fixed list of places. Anything personal it suggests waits until you approve it (you can untick anything first), and then it only moves or renames the file or sends it to the Recycle Bin. Sweepwise never empties the Recycle Bin.
help.3.a: Open History & Undo and press Undo on that run. Files go back where they were, things in the Recycle Bin are restored, startup programs switch back on and settings that Speed Boost changed go back. Undo can't reverse uninstalls, app updates, Deep Clean, unsubscribes, or cleared temporary files and caches. On a Mac, removed apps go to the Trash, so Undo does bring them back.
help.4.a: Suggestions Sweepwise is not allowed to act on by itself. Some come ticked, like junk files and chat or game apps that start by themselves, but everything waits until you press Approve, and you can untick anything first. If you untick something that came ticked and press Approve, it remembers: once, and it starts unticked next time; twice, and it is tucked away under hidden items.
help.5.q: Why does Full Scan wait before it starts?
help.5.a: A full virus scan works your PC hard for 30 to 90 minutes, and Windows won't let it be paused once it starts. If Sweepwise can read your PC's temperature, it waits until your PC is under 70 degrees C with enough free memory, so it doesn't overheat; if it can't, the scan starts straight away. A laptop on a hard surface or a stand stays cooler.
help.6.a: It runs Microsoft's own Disk Cleanup for system files and removes old Windows Update leftovers. Windows asks for permission first. What it clears is gone for good, but it never empties your Recycle Bin and never touches Downloads.
help.7.q: Do I need the AI helper?
help.7.a: No. Without it you get everything except the AI Organizer, the chat and the AI suggestions. Those use your own Claude or OpenAI key, and then the AI company (never the developer) gets names, sizes and dates, Sweepwise's own results, your recent apps and folders, your notes, what you type and, for email, senders and subject lines, but never what is inside your files. Names and subjects with private-looking words (like bank, tax or passport) are left out. Settings has a step-by-step guide to getting a key.
help.8.a: No. There is no account, no tracking and no analytics. On its own, Sweepwise only checks GitHub once a day for a newer version (you can switch this off in Settings). Scan & Clean and the Security check also ask your system's own update tools about updates, and those tools may go online. The AI, email, Unsubscribe and virus-list updates connect only when you use them.
help.9.q: Where did my moved files go?
help.9.a: Sorted files go to folders in Documents (Finance, Career, Notes and so on), Pictures, Videos and Music, and new installers to Downloads\Installers. Files Sweepwise wasn't sure about go to Documents\_Review, and files whose names look like passwords, keys or ID documents to the hidden Documents\_Private. History & Undo lists your recent runs, and Undo on a run puts its moves back.
help.10.q: Why does Windows warn me when I install Sweepwise?
help.10.a: The download from GitHub isn't signed with a paid certificate yet, so Windows shows "Windows protected your PC". Click More info, then Run anyway.
help.11.a: Yes: every feature, for everyone, with no ads and no paid version. It's kept going by people who choose to support it. Supporting is optional and unlocks nothing extra.
help.12.a: Switch off the weekly reminder and auto-clean, then uninstall Sweepwise from Windows Settings > Apps. Ticking "Delete the application data" while uninstalling also deletes its records folder.
help.13.q: Something went wrong. What should I do?
help.13.a: Files Sweepwise moved can be put back from History & Undo, and so can files it sent to the Recycle Bin while they are still there. Then report the problem on GitHub: say what you did and what happened, and please leave out personal file names.

about.licence.title: Free, and open source
about.licence.desc: Sweepwise is free. Its code is open source under the GNU General Public License, version 3, so anyone can use it, study it, share it and change it. Anyone who shares a changed version must share their code under the same licence, so Sweepwise can never be taken closed and sold.
about.warranty: Sweepwise comes with absolutely no warranty, to the extent permitted by law. Made by AlbertanCoder.
about.promise.1: Nothing personal changes without your OK.
about.promise.2: Changes you approve can be undone, except uninstalls and app updates.
about.promise.3: Your own files are never deleted for good: they are only moved or sent to the Recycle Bin, and Sweepwise never empties it.
about.promise.4: Windows repairs and system clean-ups use Microsoft's own tools, and Sweepwise clears temp files and caches itself: no registry cleaners, no tricks.

guide.title: How to get an AI key
guide.claude.1: Open Anthropic's key page (button below) and sign up or sign in.
guide.claude.2: In Billing, add a small amount of credit. How long it lasts depends on how much you use the AI.
guide.claude.3: In Limits, set a monthly spending limit (for example US$5) so you stay in control of what it costs.
guide.claude.4: In API keys, press Create key, name it Sweepwise, and copy the key. It starts with sk-ant-.
guide.claude.5: Back in Sweepwise, paste it into the AI key box and press Save and check key. The check is free.
guide.openai.1: Open OpenAI's key page (button below) and sign up or sign in.
guide.openai.2: In Billing, add a payment method or a small amount of credit.
guide.openai.3: In Limits, set a monthly budget (for example US$5) so you stay in control of what it costs.
guide.openai.4: In API keys, press Create new secret key, name it Sweepwise, and copy the key. It starts with sk-.
guide.openai.5: Back in Sweepwise, paste it into the AI key box and press Save and check key. The check is free.
guide.cost: What the AI costs goes on your own account with Anthropic or OpenAI, never on Sweepwise, and depends on how much you use it. Your key is kept encrypted on this PC and only ever sent to its own service.
sub.boost: Make your PC feel new again: fewer programs starting with Windows, less junk, lighter settings on slow PCs and up-to-date apps. Find speed-ups runs a Scan & Clean, which clears temp files and caches; everything else waits for your OK, and bigger changes wait for a Windows restore point.

set.auto.desc: Off unless you switch it on. Every Sunday at 5 pm Sweepwise quietly clears temporary files and caches only: never your files, never moves anything. Each one shows in History.
set.storage_sense.title: Storage Sense
set.storage_sense.desc: Windows' own automatic clean-up. If you turn it on in Windows Settings, check it is not set to empty your Recycle Bin or Downloads unless you want that.
set.drivers.title: Driver updates
set.drivers.desc: For drivers, use Windows Update (optional updates). Sweepwise never uses third-party driver tools.
set.auto_link.desc: Temporary files and caches only, every Sunday, if you switch it on on the Speed Boost page.
habits.desc: Learned on this PC only, from the files and apps you open. Scan & Clean won't suggest binning a file you opened in the last two weeks (unless it is an exact copy) and marks it when it suggests a move. The AI only ever sees folder and app names.
sub.email: Clears old newsletters and promotions out of your inbox. Sweepwise reads only the top lines of each email (sender, subject, date and the like), never what your emails say. It skips people you wrote to in the past year and mail that looks like bank, government or health mail, security alerts or receipts, spotted by keywords, so look over the list. Everything goes to your own Trash, and Undo puts it back while it is still there.

guide.app.title: How to make an app password
guide.gmail.1: Your Google account needs 2-Step Verification turned on (Google Account > Security).
guide.gmail.2: Open Google's app passwords page (button below) and sign in.
guide.gmail.3: Type Sweepwise as the name and press Create.
guide.gmail.4: Copy the 16-letter password Google shows (the spaces do not matter).
guide.gmail.5: Back in Sweepwise, pick Gmail, type your Gmail address, paste the app password and press Connect.
guide.yahoo.1: Open Yahoo's account security page (button below) and sign in.
guide.yahoo.2: Choose Generate app password (or App passwords).
guide.yahoo.3: Type Sweepwise as the name and press Generate.
guide.yahoo.5: Back in Sweepwise, pick Yahoo, type your Yahoo address, paste the app password and press Connect.
guide.icloud.1: Open Apple's account page (button below) and sign in.
guide.icloud.2: In Sign-In and Security, choose App-Specific Passwords and press +.
guide.icloud.3: Type Sweepwise as the name and press Create.
guide.icloud.5: Back in Sweepwise, pick iCloud, type your iCloud address (@icloud.com or @me.com), paste the app password and press Connect.
guide.app.note: Sweepwise uses an app password only to sign in to your email, and keeps it encrypted on this PC. You can delete it on your provider's page any time; Sweepwise then stops working with that account.
sub.secSub@linux: ClamAV does the virus scanning on Linux. Sweepwise checks it is installed and up to date, checks your firewall and safety switches, and looks for things that should not be there. This check only reads; it changes nothing.
tile.clean_check_and_repair_windows.desc: On systems that use apt (like Ubuntu, Debian and Linux Mint), also lets the package manager finish any software installs that were interrupted. Adds a minute or two.
tile.clean_system_files.desc@linux: Downloaded package files, system logs older than two weeks and old switched-off snap versions. A few minutes. Never empties your Trash or touches Downloads.
tile.deep_clean.desc@linux: System files only an admin can clear. Asks for your password.
tile.optimize.desc@linux: Programs that start when you sign in, each with a plain suggestion.
tile.quick_scan.desc@linux: If ClamAV is installed, it checks Downloads, Desktop and the other places viruses usually hide. A few minutes.
help.1.a@linux: It clears caches that Linux and your apps make and never tidy up (picture previews, Python's download cache and browser caches), runs a quick virus scan if ClamAV is installed, and checks your computer's health. Then it lists anything else it suggests (files to tidy, old AI leftovers, startup programs, apps) and waits for your OK. The very first time, it shows what it would remove and waits for you to press Clean now.
help.5.a@linux: A full virus scan with ClamAV works your computer hard and can take an hour or more. If Sweepwise can read the temperature, it waits until your computer is under 70 degrees C with enough free memory, so it doesn't overheat; if it can't, the scan starts straight away. A laptop on a hard surface or a stand stays cooler.
help.6.a@linux: It clears downloaded package files, system logs older than two weeks and old switched-off snap versions for good, with admin rights (your system asks for your password). If Timeshift is installed, it tries to make a snapshot first. It never empties your Trash and never touches Downloads.
help.9.a@linux: Sorted files go to folders in Documents (Finance, Career, Notes and so on), Pictures, Videos and Music, and new installers to Downloads/Installers. Files Sweepwise wasn't sure about go to Documents/_Review, and files whose names look like passwords, keys or ID documents to a separate Documents/_Private folder. History & Undo lists your recent runs, and Undo on a run puts its moves back.
help.10.q@linux: Which Linux versions does Sweepwise work on?
help.10.a@linux: There is a .deb package for Ubuntu, Linux Mint and Debian, and an AppImage to try on other systems, such as Fedora. So far only automatic checks have tested it, on Ubuntu 22.04. Some checks need tools your system may not have, so a few items may be left out or say what is missing.
help.12.a@linux: Switch off the weekly reminder and auto-clean, then remove Sweepwise the way you installed it: your Software app, "sudo apt remove sweepwise" for the .deb, or delete the AppImage file. Also delete its records folder (you can open it from this page). If you saved a key or password, a small Sweepwise entry may stay in your keyring.
about.promise.4@linux: System clean-ups and updates use your system's own tools (apt, Flatpak, journalctl, ClamAV), and Sweepwise clears caches itself: no tricks.
sub.boost@linux: Make your computer feel new again: fewer programs starting when you sign in, less junk, lighter settings on slow computers and up-to-date apps. Find speed-ups runs a Scan & Clean, which clears caches; everything else waits for your OK, and if Timeshift is installed, bigger changes wait for a snapshot.
help.14.q: Can I tell Sweepwise which email senders to always keep or always clean?
help.14.a: Yes. In Sweepwise's own records folder (About & privacy > Open Sweepwise's own records), make a text file called email-keep.txt and/or email-clean.txt with one email address or domain per line. Senders on the keep list are never suggested. Senders on the clean list are suggested and ticked when they have inbox emails over 30 days old that aren't starred, unless you unticked them before. People you wrote to in the past year, and addresses that look like a bank or government, are never suggested.
sub.secSub@mac: XProtect and Gatekeeper, built into macOS, do the malware protection. Sweepwise checks they are on, checks FileVault, the firewall and sharing, and looks for things that should not be there. ClamAV can be added to scan your files. This check only reads; it changes nothing.
tile.clean_check_and_repair_windows.desc: Also runs Disk Utility's read-only check of your startup disk. Adds a few minutes.
tile.clean_system_files.desc@mac: System log archives and crash reports older than two weeks. A few minutes. Never empties your Trash or touches Downloads.
tile.deep_clean.desc@mac: Old system files only an admin can clear. Asks for your password.
tile.optimize.desc@mac: Programs that start when you sign in, each with a plain suggestion.
tile.quick_scan.desc@mac: If ClamAV is installed, it checks Downloads, Desktop and the other places harmful files usually land. XProtect already checks apps when they open.
help.1.a@mac: It clears caches that macOS and your apps make and never tidy up, runs a quick virus scan if ClamAV is installed, and checks your Mac's health. Then it lists anything else it suggests (files to tidy, old AI leftovers, startup programs, apps you don't use) and waits for your OK. The very first time, it shows what it would remove and waits for you to press Clean now.
help.5.a@mac: A full virus scan with ClamAV works your Mac hard and can take an hour or more. If Sweepwise can read your Mac's temperature, it waits until your Mac is under 70 degrees C with enough free memory, so it doesn't overheat; if it can't, the scan starts straight away.
help.6.a@mac: It clears system log archives and crash reports older than two weeks for good, with admin rights (macOS asks for your password). Time Machine makes a snapshot first when it can. It never empties your Trash and never touches Downloads.
help.9.a@mac: Sorted files go to folders in Documents (Finance, Career, Notes and so on), Pictures, Movies and Music, and new installers to Downloads/Installers. Files Sweepwise wasn't sure about go to Documents/_Review, and files whose names look like passwords, keys or ID documents to a separate Documents/_Private folder. History & Undo lists your recent runs, and Undo on a run puts its moves back.
help.10.q@mac: Why does my Mac say Sweepwise cannot be opened?
help.10.a@mac: Until Apple has checked (notarized) Sweepwise, macOS asks before opening it the first time. Open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll down and click Open Anyway.
help.12.a@mac: Switch off the weekly reminder and auto-clean, then drag Sweepwise from Applications to the Trash. Also delete its records folder (you can open it from this page). If you saved a key or password, a small Sweepwise item may stay in Keychain Access.
about.promise.4@mac: Mac maintenance uses macOS's own tools (launchctl, Spotlight, Time Machine, Software Update), plus Homebrew and ClamAV if you have them, and Sweepwise clears caches and old logs itself: no tricks.
sub.boost@mac: Make your Mac feel new again: fewer apps starting when you sign in, less junk, unused apps moved to the Trash and up-to-date Homebrew apps. Find speed-ups runs a Scan & Clean, which clears caches; everything else waits for your OK, and app updates wait for a Time Machine snapshot.
